# Field and marine research under real constraints {#sec-session-07}

**Meeting 7 | Tuesday, October 20, 2026 | 1:00-2:00 PM Pacific**

## Central question

How do logistics, sampling opportunities, institutions, and irreproducible environments shape the questions scientists can investigate?

## The paper pair

**Pairing type:** Local field history / collective observing infrastructure.

### Paper A: The Rigours of an Arctic Experiment: The Precarious Authority of Field Practices in the Canadian High Arctic, 1958--1970

@powell2007. **Environment and Planning A (2007).** [Paper / publisher record](https://doi.org/10.1068/a38294)

Read Powell’s introduction, one field episode, and conclusion.

*Access: Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.*

### Paper B: Fifty Years of Scientific Ocean Drilling

@becker2019. **Oceanography (2019).** [Paper / publisher record](https://tos.org/oceanography/article/fifty-years-of-scientific-ocean-drilling) | [DOI](https://doi.org/10.5670/oceanog.2019.110)

Read the short scientific-ocean-drilling overview in full.

*Access: Free publisher article and PDF link.*

### Why these papers belong together

Powell draws on archival and oral-history material; Becker and colleagues give a collective retrospective of an observing program. Compare scales of practice without mistaking a program overview for a contemporaneous shipboard log. [@powell2007; @becker2019]

## Prepare before the meeting

Bring a proposal plan and a nonconfidential account of what actually happened in a lab, field, or marine campaign.

## Discussion questions

1. Which campaign deviations change the scientific interpretation, not just efficiency?
2. What survives as a reusable sample, measurement, or archive?
3. How should an agent respond when the planned observation becomes impossible?

## One-hour meeting

| Time | Activity |
|:--|:--|
| 0-10 min | Independent first judgments; surface disagreements. |
| 10-25 min | Compare the papers: claim, evidence, assumptions, and limits. |
| 25-45 min | Work through the case exercise below. |
| 45-55 min | Translate the discussion into agent requirements and tests. |
| 55-60 min | Record an output and one unresolved disagreement. |

### Case exercise

Compare planned questions, observations actually obtained, contingencies, revised strategy, and claims ultimately warranted. Introduce one constraint such as lost ship time or an instrument failure and require an explicit scientific tradeoff rather than a silent plan change.

## Agent-design or evaluation output

Adaptive observation plan: prioritized evidence, feasible substitutes, provenance of deviations, unanswerable questions, and stopping conditions.

## Record after the meeting

Record the evidence for your main claim, what changed your mind, what remains unresolved, and one change to the agent or its evaluation. Keep confidential examples in private group notes rather than committing them to this public book.
